recommendations.why: Checks whether the rate of one outcome, such as conversion, differs between two groups. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: some groups have only a handful of successes or failures
there are more than two groups or more than two outcomes
the outcome is a numeric measure rather than a yes/no rate

recommendations.why: Splits the rows into one group per distinct value of a field, such as one group per region or per answer option. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the field is a number you want in bands, not one group per value
the field is a date and you want months or quarters
the field is a multi-select answer

recommendations.why: Labels each row with the named date range its date falls in, such as custom fiscal quarters or before and after a launch. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: plain calendar months, quarters or weeks are enough
you want to keep only the rows inside the ranges

recommendations.why: Checks whether the average of a numeric measure differs across three or more groups. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the groups have clearly unequal spread
the measure is heavily skewed or only ordered
the same subjects are measured in every group
there are only two groups
you need to know which pairs of groups differ

follow_ups.when: the groups differ and you want to know which pairs of groups do
the groups are the rows of a crosstab of averages and you want every pair tested

recommendations.why: Checks whether the average of a numeric measure differs across groups when the groups may have unequal spread. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the measure is heavily skewed or only ordered
the same subjects are measured in every group
there are only two groups, or you want pairwise follow-ups: run TEST_WELCH per pair and set multiplicity on the request (for example holm) to adjust their p-values for multiple comparisons
spreads are similar and you want Tukey's pairwise follow-up

follow_ups.when: the groups differ and you want each pair tested without assuming equal spread
the groups differ and their spreads turn out similar after all

recommendations.why: Checks whether two categorical fields are associated by comparing a cross-tabulation with the counts expected if unrelated. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the table is 2x2 and some expected counts are small
you compare a yes/no rate between exactly two groups and want a confidence interval
both fields are numeric
you compare one subgroup's mix with the whole population

follow_ups.when: the table shows an association and you want to see which cells drive it
you want to see which rows depart from the overall column mix

recommendations.why: Exact test of whether two yes/no fields are associated, built for small 2x2 tables. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: either field has more than two categories
counts are large and you want the difference in rates with a confidence interval

recommendations.why: Rank-based check of whether values tend to be larger in some groups than in others, across two or more groups. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the data are roughly normal and you want to compare averages
there are only two groups
the same subjects are measured in every group and the measure is roughly normal (Pulse has no Friedman test for skewed repeated measures; for two conditions use TEST_WILCOXON_SR)

follow_ups.when: the groups differ and you want a rank-based comparison of each pair, read with multiple-comparison caution

recommendations.why: Checks whether a numeric field's values follow the same distribution in two groups, comparing their whole shape. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: you want to check one field against the normal distribution
you only care whether one group's values tend to be larger
you compare a subgroup with the whole population

recommendations.why: Rank-based check of whether values in one of two groups tend to be larger than in the other. Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

alternatives.when: the same subjects are measured twice
there are three or more groups
the data are roughly normal and you want the difference in averages
you care about any difference in the shape of the two distributions
